sections.title: The Commissioning of the Twelve Apostles
observations: In this section, Jesus calls His twelve disciples and gives them authority to heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those who have leprosy, and drive out demons. This commissioning signifies the beginning of their ministry and the establishment of the church's mission.

The specific instructions given to the apostles emphasize reliance on God for provision and the urgency of their mission. They are to go to the lost sheep of Israel, indicating a focus on the Jewish people before the gospel is extended to the Gentiles.

sections.title: Instructions for the Mission
observations: Jesus provides detailed instructions on how the apostles are to conduct themselves during their mission. They are to preach the message of the kingdom, heal the sick, and demonstrate the power of God.
The emphasis on going without extra provisions teaches the apostles to trust in God’s provision and the hospitality of those they encounter. This reliance on God is a key theme in the Christian life.

sections.title: Persecution and Suffering
observations: Jesus warns the apostles that they will face persecution and hostility. He prepares them for the reality that following Him may lead to suffering and rejection.
The call to take up one's cross is a central theme in discipleship. Jesus reassures them that they are not alone and that the Spirit will speak through them in times of trial.

sections.title: The Cost of Discipleship
observations: In this section, Jesus speaks about the cost of following Him. He emphasizes that loyalty to Him must surpass all other relationships, even family ties.
This radical call to discipleship challenges the cultural norms of the time and continues to challenge believers today. It invites reflection on what it means to truly follow Christ.

sections.title: Rewards for Disciples
observations: Jesus concludes this chapter by speaking about the rewards for those who receive the apostles and the message they bring. He highlights the importance of hospitality and support for those in ministry.
The promise of reward for even the smallest act of kindness towards a disciple underscores the value of every believer's contribution to the kingdom.

importantVerses.commentary: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those who have leprosy, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
Whoever acknowledges me before others, I will also acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it.

questions: What does it mean to be sent out as sheep among wolves?
How can we apply the principle of relying on God’s provision in our own lives?
What does Jesus mean when He says that He came to bring a sword?
In what ways can we demonstrate hospitality to those in ministry today?
How do we reconcile the call to love our families with the call to prioritize our relationship with Christ?
